meta.note: Three references chosen to triangulate Finla's actual position: one where-we-want-to-land (Ramp), one what-to-explicitly-avoid (Paraşüt — the direct local competitor pattern), one closest-genre-match (Cursor — conversational-AI-as-core-interface, same as ChatDemo). Hex values here are qualitative/directional, not pixel-measured (WebFetch returns markdown-converted text, not rendered CSS/screenshots) — reference-dna.json is meant to steer taste and structure in Faz 2, not to be copied literally. Grounded via WebFetch content-structure fetches (2026-09-03) plus known public design identity of each product.

meta.name: Ramp (ramp.com)
meta.description: Global corporate-card/spend-management fintech. Chosen as the 'serious fintech that refuses to look boring' aspiration point — closest to what Finla should feel like as a category, several steps more mature/funded than Finla but directionally correct.

color.palette_type: monochromatic with a single sharp accent (historically a saturated blue/violet, used sparingly)

accent.hex: single saturated accent (blue/violet family), used only for emphasis (links, key CTA, chart highlights)

neutral.usage: text hierarchy and card backgrounds only

color.contrast_strategy: high-contrast dark-on-light dominant, near-monochrome outside the one accent

typography.font_style_notes: confident, oversized display type carrying most of the visual weight; grotesque/geometric sans; quantified claims ('7x fewer clicks') set at heading scale, not buried in body copy

spacing.section_rhythm: modular — each product line gets its own full-bleed section with a consistent capability→control→use-case rhythm

components.component_notes: product screenshots (real UI, not illustration) are the primary visual proof; feature sections repeat a strict 3-part pattern (claim, mechanism, concrete outcome)

aesthetic.genre: engineering-led fintech, closer to a dev-tool than a bank

overview.primary_technology: CSS + light JS, real product screenshots over ambient decoration

references.takeaway_for_finla: Real product proof (Ramp uses real screenshots; Finla has ChatDemo) beats decoration. Quantified, concrete claims set at real visual weight — Finla's copy already has this instinct ('form doldurarak', 'Bodrum'da yazıldı') but could push numbers/outcomes harder in supporting sections, not just the hero line.

meta.name: Paraşüt (parasut.com)
meta.description: Turkey's leading SME accounting/e-fatura SaaS — direct local competitor, and the explicit anti-pattern the brief warns against ('kurumsal ve sıkıcı değil'). Included deliberately as a negative reference: this is the exact visual territory Finla must NOT drift into.

color.palette_type: complementary — teal/blue-green brand primary against warm coral/orange-peach secondary
color.contrast_strategy: conventional SaaS light-mode, no inversion sections

typography.font_style_notes: bold geometric sans headers (Montserrat-like), medium-weight body — safe, generic SaaS type system with no distinguishing character

components.component_notes: three-column feature grids, horizontal banner cards per product line, star-rating social proof widgets — textbook conventional SaaS component kit

visual_language.ornamentation: minimalist line icons + product screenshots, subtle banner gradients — nothing that couldn't be swapped onto any other SaaS product

brand_voice_in_ui.tone: professional yet approachable, mainstream KOBİ-software register ('kolaylıkla', 'zahmetsizce')

references.takeaway_for_finla: This is the trap to avoid: gradient logo + teal/coral complementary palette + 3-column feature grid + star-rating social proof is the default 'Turkish SME SaaS' visual grammar. Finla's monochrome-plus-one-accent restraint and ChatDemo-as-hero already diverge from this correctly — Faz 2/3 must not accidentally regress toward a feature-grid, multi-color, gradient-logo look chasing 'more trustworthy = more color/icons'. Paraşüt also validates that Finla's anti-corporate copy voice is a genuine differentiator in this specific market, not just a generic brand-voice choice.

meta.name: Cursor (cursor.com)
meta.description: AI coding agent. Chosen as the closest genre match for Finla's actual mechanic: the product IS a conversational AI interface, and the marketing site's job is to make that chat interaction itself the hero, not illustrate around it — exactly ChatDemo's role on heyfinla.com.

color.palette_type: monochromatic dark-mode-first with a single accent, light mode also supported

accent.role: used only where it earns attention

typography.font_style_notes: clean modern sans, large confident display headline ('Cursor is your coding agent for building ambitious software'), size contrast does the hierarchy work — not color or decoration

visual_language.focal_strategy: single hero element — an interactive/live-feeling product demo (desktop + CLI interface) is the centerpiece, not a supporting screenshot

interaction_feel.loading_style: product demo is staged as an active, in-progress interaction (agent 'building' something live), not a static screenshot

overview.primary_technology: interactive product-demo framing over ambient effects

references.takeaway_for_finla: Confirms the right instinct already in the codebase: the conversational interface itself (ChatDemo) should be staged as an active, in-progress interaction — not a static phone screenshot — exactly as ChatDemo's typewriter + tool-call-chip choreography already does. Cursor also validates dark-mode-first restraint (one dominant tone + one accent) as the correct register for 'this is a serious tool, not a consumer toy' — reinforces keeping Finla's current single-accent-green discipline in Faz 2 rather than introducing a multi-color palette.

where_current_site_is_weak: Typography is a single family (Inter) stretched across a ~17x size range via ad-hoc arbitrary values (5px–84px) rather than a formal, named type scale — Ramp and Cursor both lean on 2-3 clearly stepped display/heading/body roles with more deliberate size jumps.

No monospace/code-adjacent type token exists despite the product literally displaying tool-call names (musteri_bul, vergi_kontrol) that read like function calls — Cursor's genre uses mono accents for exactly this kind of content and it would reinforce credibility here.

Numbers/outcomes are present in the brand voice but not yet given real visual weight anywhere outside Tech's stats — Ramp sets quantified claims at heading scale as a structural pattern, which Finla's Features/Tech sections could borrow more deliberately.

Depth/shadow is currently reserved almost entirely for the hero phone mockup; the rest of the site is quite flat, which is a reasonable restraint but leaves little room for a secondary visual signature beyond the phone itself.
Stale README claim of a second display typeface (Space Grotesk) that was never actually wired in — a signal that typographic identity was intended to be more distinctive than what shipped.
where_references_are_strong: Ramp: quantified, concrete claims set at real visual weight; real product proof over decoration.
Paraşüt (negative reference): shows precisely which local-market visual clichés to avoid — gradient logos, teal+coral complementary palettes, 3-column generic feature grids, star-rating badges.
Cursor: staging the core AI interaction as an active, in-progress demo rather than a static screenshot — validates and should extend ChatDemo's existing approach rather than replace it.
comparison_notes.directional_conclusion: Finla's current restraint (monochrome + one accent, no ambient effects, product-simulation-as-hero) is already the right instinct relative to all three references — the gap is not 'add more decoration' but 'sharpen the type system, give tool-call/mono content its own typographic register, and let quantified outcomes carry more visual weight' while explicitly not drifting toward Paraşüt's conventional SaaS grammar.
